summary: Frozen subjects enumeration now complete through offset 108; links complete through offset 36. All proposed citations and upstream contradiction evidence independently read. proposed_facts.reason: The helper installs BLR, flushes 20 bytes and invokes the array with the declared by-value u128 argument. Accept the explicit deferral of how the FPSCR sequence obtains its r4 scratch address.
Canonical classification ignores instruction-read and posting results. The event implementation initializes the stated fields and copies into its two-entry queue only when not full.

Pending input sets inputActivated and restores monitor context; the continuation clears the flag without posting. The saved LR, targcont.c continuation and main-loop input handling support the cross-file account.
Extended1 writes set restore flags before reading replacements. The restore consumer clears both flags, conditionally restores the time base and unconditionally branches past the DEC write.

The upper-bound rejection precedes state changes. Reversed direct-call ranges leave error uninitialized, while protocol handlers reject reversed operands. Exception and restore-flag ordering match the proposal.

Extended2 performs unguarded HID2/GQR0 preparation, overwrites intermediate transfer errors and counts attempted iterations. Its local cleanup restores exception status, not live setup registers or transferred data.
FP preparation precedes the range loop, including empty ranges. Both stages run per iteration with error overwrites; the function restores exception status but not the live MSR or transferred data.

Nested debugger recovery records PC and exception ID separately from gTRKCPUState. The exception serializer reads instruction memory at that recorded PC rather than obtaining an instruction from the snapshot.
TRKTargetCheckStep returns remaining activity. False, including newly completed stepping, triggers stopped state and notification.
The handler's switch, false-result notification guard and default success return directly establish the corrected state behavior.

Command and handle narrowing, ignored posting failure and unconditional post-service actions match the source. The service's early parameter rejection precedes io_result initialization, supporting the undefined-result caveat.

The validator uses inclusive-end arithmetic, truncated selector tests, first-overlap selection and the stated suffix boundary. The configured map spans the full 32-bit address space; neither generic complete coverage nor physical safety follows.

contradictions.reason: Accept deferral of all five .bss-attributed facts and both .bss links. Declarations and context exchanges support named objects' roles but do not prove compiled membership. Absolute-address OS-thread declarations further preclude inferring placement from missing initializers. Pending-input restoration returns to monitor processing without posting a target event.

Accept deferral of all five .data-attributed facts and the .data link. Initial states and object roles are supported, but section membership, 48-byte size, padding and blanket safety are not established. Restore flags do not guarantee DEC restoration.
Accept deferral of the .rodata fact and link. The map declaration and mutable local instruction arrays establish functionality, not compiled map placement or emitted template contents.
The scratch-address ABI claim is not established by the by-value source declaration. Proposal 0 preserves observable execution while explicitly deferring compiled ABI verification.
Guaranteed event enqueue and pending-event processing accounts are corrected by proposals 1 and 2: reads and posts can fail unchecked, and inputActivated suppresses posting entirely.

Proposals 3 and 4 correct the Extended1 hardware-restoration guarantee and add consequential failure paths: flags precede buffer reads, DEC restoration is skipped, and reversed direct calls can return an uninitialized error despite protocol range checks.

Proposals 5 and 6 clarify that loop guards do not success-guard both transfer stages. Intermediate errors are overwritten, attempted iterations are counted, and live setup state is not restored locally.

Proposal 7 resolves the conflation of debugger-internal exception reporting with ordinary stopped-target reporting and correctly distinguishes recorded fields from the instruction fetched at report time.
Proposals 8 and 9 resolve both inverted step-completion claims: completion clears active, so completed stepping permits rather than suppresses the stop notification.
Proposal 10 resolves guaranteed posting and result-normalization claims. Queue posting can fail, and early service rejection leaves the caller's local I/O result uninitialized.

Proposal 11 resolves the overly strong recursive-coverage account. The suffix rechecks map.end, selector values outside the two tested values bypass permission rejection, and zero length has no explicit guard. The actual full-space map does not prove physical accessibility.
